    RuleFit Model Objects

    rule_ensemble-object.Rd

    rule_ensemble(), rule_ensemble_xgb(), rule_ensemble_lgb(), and rule_ensemble_ctb() return a list with class "rule_ensemble". This page describes its elements.

    Classes

    The first class is specific to the boosting library and is followed by "rule_ensemble", "hardhat_model", and "hardhat_scalar". The first class is "rule_ensemble_xgb", "rule_ensemble_lgb", or "rule_ensemble_ctb" for xgboost, lightgbm, and catboost, respectively. Methods such as predict(), tidy(), and multi_predict() are defined for the "rule_ensemble" class.

    Elements

    • rules: A tibble (a rule_set object from the lorax package) with one row per rule that was retained for the glmnet model. Rules with a single unique value in the training set, or that are linear combinations of other columns, are removed. The columns are:

      • tree: The integer index of the tree that the rule came from.

      • rules: A list column of R expressions that define the rule (e.g., wt <= 2.26 & qsec <= 19.17). Use show_rule() to print one.

      • id: The integer identifier of the tree node that defines the rule.

      • label: A character column of rule names (e.g., "rule_01"). These are the column names of the rule indicators in the glmnet model. The labels are made before rules are removed, so they may not be consecutive.

    • fit: A parsnip model_fit object of the glmnet model. The predictors are the original predictors (with indicator columns for factors) and one 0/1 column per rule. A numeric outcome uses parsnip::linear_reg(), a factor with two levels uses parsnip::logistic_reg(), and a factor with more levels uses parsnip::multinom_reg().

    • arguments: A named list of the values used to fit the model. It contains the main arguments (trees, mtry, learn_rate, tree_depth, min_n, penalty, mixture, and verbose) followed by any boosting and glmnet options. min_n is not included for catboost models.

    • blueprint: The hardhat blueprint used to process new data with hardhat::forge(). Its type depends on the type of x used to fit the model (data frame, matrix, formula, or recipe).

    • training: A list with information about the training set:

      • rows: The number of rows used to fit the glmnet model. For lightgbm, rows with missing values in the predictor or rule columns are removed first.

      • ptype: A zero-row data frame of the processed predictors, with character columns converted to factors. It is used to make the same indicator columns for new data.

      • weights: NULL when case weights were not used. Otherwise, the type of case weights: "frequency", "importance", or "numeric" (a plain numeric vector).

    Examples

    if (rlang::is_installed(c("modeldata", "xgboost"))) {
  data(two_class_dat, package = "modeldata")

  fit <- rule_ensemble(Class ~ ., data = two_class_dat, trees = 5)
  class(fit)
  names(fit)

  fit$rules
  str(fit$training)
}
#> List of 3
#>  $ rows   : int 791
#>  $ ptype  : tibble [0 × 2] (S3: tbl_df/tbl/data.frame)
#>   ..$ A: num(0) 
#>   ..$ B: num(0) 
#>  $ weights: NULL
